title: cohort-credit-allocator-and-failure-proxy-for-regression-attribution
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Adds cohort-level credit assignment for failures and a lightweight failure-proxy that surfaces attributed regression signals to CI and alerting. Non-breaking feature behind runtime flag.
description:
Motivation: We've observed noisy regression alerts that are difficult to prioritize because failures are often shared across overlapping prompt cohorts, model variants, and prompt-version edits. This PR implements a 'cohort credit allocator' that attributes a fraction of a failure to competing explanatory axes (prompt cohort, prompt-version, model-variant, and recent prompt edits) and exposes those attributions via a small failure-proxy endpoint that CI hooks and the alerting pipeline can consume.

Design summary: The feature has two components: (1) cohort-credit-allocator - a deterministic, explainable algorithm that takes event-level traces from eval runs and returns an attribution vector normalized to 1. Attribution heuristics include temporal proximity to edits, cohort overlap score, and agreement across seeded reruns; weights are tunable via config. (2) failure-proxy - an HTTP shim that aggregates eval-run failure events, enriches them with attribution metadata from the allocator, stores compact rollup blobs to S3 (or internal blobstore), and emits a compact webhook payload for CI/alerting. The allocator runs as part of eval post-processing and is opt-in per-eval via a flag.

What changed (high level files): src/allocator/crediting.py - core attribution logic and unit tests; src/proxy/failure_proxy.py - lightweight FastAPI shim and delivery code; infra/ci/hooks/failure-attribution-webhook.yaml - CI hook wiring; tests/integration/test_crediting_end_to_end.py - integration test using a synthetic prompt-cohort bundle; docs/ops/failure-attribution.md - operational runbook and config knobs; examples/cohorts/sample_cohort_v2.json - example input.

Commits (summary):
- 8f3a7b7  feat(allocator): implement baseline credit allocator and deterministic tie-breaker
- 7ed2c44  test(allocator): add unit tests for overlap and time-decay heuristics
- d3b9f11  feat(proxy): add failure-proxy FastAPI shim + S3 rollups
- 4b1a662  ci: wire webhook to integration-stage evaluations
- b8c0d90  docs: add ops guide and rollout notes
- c2ee901  fix(tests): stabilize flaky integration test by seeding RNG

Testing and CI: Initial CI run surfaced a flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_crediting_end_to_end.py) caused by nondeterministic seed usage. I patched seeding and added a retry wrapper for the integration runner. The first CI run showed one failed job (integration/e2e) and two flaky warnings; after the fix and force-push the full CI passed (unit, lint, mypy, integration/e2e). The ci_status is pass.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Aisha Gupta (reviewer): "Nice shape. Two asks: (1) Can we add a short note about complexity (O(n*m)) in doc and guard large cohorts? (2) Add a config knob so we can disable time-decay for certain datasets."
- Author (Priya): "Answered both: added cohort_size guard in config with default 10k and added decay_enabled flag. See allocator config in docs and default.yaml."
- Miguel Torres: "One API nit: failure-proxy should return a consistent schema even when attribution is empty. Also add a healthcheck endpoint for readiness."
- Author: "Updated FastAPI to always return attribution: [] and added /_healthz and /_ready endpoints. Integration tests exercise the readiness path."
- Evan Kim: "Approving pending small doc wording change on ops guide."
- Evan Kim (later): "Approved".

Performance considerations: The allocator runs as an offline postprocess step per-eval; we've added a cohort_size cutoff and sampling path so memory usage stays bounded. A microbenchmark included in tests shows <300ms additional wallclock for a 2k-item eval run on the standard runner; heavy workloads will use the sampling/approximate path.

Backward compatibility and flags: Default behavior is unchanged unless eval-run has the flag attribution.enabled=true. The failure-proxy is behind a feature gate (env var FAILURE_PROXY_ENABLED). Ops doc documents how to flip the gate and the safe rollout plan.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable flag in staging for daily smoke evals (1 week), 2) route CI webhook to an internal Slack channel for triage (2 weeks), 3) enable in canary for 10% of nightly evals (3 weeks), 4) full rollout and turn on alert scoring thresholds. Feature can be disabled instantly via env var or eval flags.

Known limitations and future work: Current allocator uses a small set of heuristics; future work includes learned attribution models, integration with the regression blame tool, and surfacing per-token saliency when available. The proxy payload is deliberately compact to keep CI payload sizes small; a follow-up will add an endpoint for expanded diagnostics.

Merge details: After approvals from Aisha, Miguel, and Evan and a green CI run, this was merged via squash-merge. The squash commit message contains a short summary and Linear links.

Files changed (high level): ["src/allocator/crediting.py", "src/allocator/config.py", "src/proxy/failure_proxy.py", "infra/ci/hooks/failure-attribution-webhook.yaml", "tests/unit/test_crediting.py", "tests/integration/test_crediting_end_to_end.py", "docs/ops/failure-attribution.md", "examples/cohorts/sample_cohort_v2.json", "examples/cohorts/README.md"].

Notes for on-call: The ops doc includes recommended thresholds for alerting (credit > 0.5 on a single cohort across 3 runs) and a short playbook to disable the proxy and re-run attribution on demand.

Related work: This PR is complementary to ENG-3578 (regression blamer) and should reduce false-positive volume in the regression triage queue by surfacing more precise signals.

If you want to try locally: run `PYTHONPATH=. pytest tests/integration/test_crediting_end_to_end.py -k fast` and then run `examples/run_local_eval.sh --with-attribution` to see proxy payloads in the local sink.
